blocks.text: What is the Constitution?

blocks.text: What is the Indian Parliament?
The Indian Parliament is the supreme legislative body in India. It is a bicameral legislature, consisting of two houses: the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.

The Lok Sabha, also known as the House of the People, has 543 elected members. The Rajya Sabha, or the Council of States, has 245 members, with 233 elected by the state legislatures and 12 nominated by the President.

items: The Indian Parliament is a bicameral legislature
The Lok Sabha has 543 elected members
The Rajya Sabha has 245 members
The Parliament makes laws for the country

steps.title: How a Bill becomes a Law
steps.body: A bill is introduced in either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha, and then it is debated and voted upon. If it is passed, it is sent to the other house for approval. If both houses pass the bill, it is sent to the President for signature.

blocks.text: Common mistake: The President of India has the power to reject a bill, but this power is rarely used. However, the President can return a bill to the Parliament for reconsideration.

items.q: What is the difference between the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha?

items.q: How are the members of the Parliament elected?
items.a: The members of the Lok Sabha are elected by the people of India, while the members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by the state legislatures.

items.a: The President has the power to sign a bill into law, but can also return it to the Parliament for reconsideration.

blocks.text: Introduction to GDP
GDP stands for Gross Domestic Product, which is the total value of goods and services produced within a country's borders. It is a key indicator of a country's economic growth and development.

India's GDP is calculated by the Central Statistical Office (CSO) using the following formula: GDP = C + I + G + (X - M), where C is consumption, I is investment, G is government spending, X is exports, and M is imports.
